description: Pre-signed URL Abuse Through Extended Access The web server generates pre-signed URLs for S3 operations without enforcing short expiration times. These URLs remain valid until expiration, potentially allowing unauthorized access if intercepted or shared. An attacker who obtains a pre-signed URL could access the associated S3 object repeatedly until the URL expires, even if the original user's session has ended or their access should have been revoked.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
recommendation: Implement strict expiration times for pre-signed URLs
recommendation: Implement URL tracking and revocation capability

description: Pre-signed URL Interception and Unauthorized Usage Pre-signed URLs may be intercepted during transmission through man-in-the-middle attacks, network sniffing, or client-side security issues. An attacker on the same network could intercept pre-signed URLs through network sniffing, or exploit vulnerable client-side storage to harvest URLs.
references: recommendation: Enforce HTTPS throughout the application stack
recommendation: Implement request signing and validation

description: Insufficient Network Segmentation Leading to Data Exfiltration Overly permissive security group rules and lack of network segmentation could allow unauthorized network traversal and data access. An attacker who compromises the EC2 instance could use it as a pivot point to access other resources or exfiltrate data from the S3 bucket due to the instance's IAM permissions.
references: recommendation: Implement strict security group rules
recommendation: Implement least privilege IAM policies
